Tiszabercel Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tiszabercel, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews settled in Tiszabercel at the end of the 18th century, peaking at 259 residents by 1820 before declining to 129 by 1944. The community joined the Orthodox stream after 1869's Schism, building a new synagogue at the century's end. Rabbi Ede Fried, who also served Buj and Ibrány, was murdered at Auschwitz alongside most of his congregation. Immediately after Passover 1944, following German occupation, the community was sent to the overcrowded Nyíregyháza Ghetto, enduring hunger and shortages before deportation weeks later. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1859, its newest to 1943.
